newsitem.title: USA: PSA eyes SEC plan to revamp trading system rules.
newsitem.headline: PSA eyes SEC plan to revamp trading system rules.

text.p: A group of bond market participants will begin studying on Monday the market impact of a Securities and Exchange Commission plan to revamp regulation of stock exchanges and computer trading systems.

The 22-member, newly-formed group was established by bond market trade association PSA and will be chaired by Christopher Carroll, managing director, Global Electronic Trading at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The PSA panel's efforts come only weeks after the SEC decided to develop massive changes in how it regulates exchanges and so-called alternative trading systems.

"One concern I have about the SEC's concept release is that it speaks eloquently about how to regulate alternative trading systems, but it really doesn't go into any kind of depth about why they should be regulated in the first place," Paul Saltzman, PSA's general counsel, told Reuters.
PSA feels "fairly strongly" that the debt markets are "more than adequately" regulated, he said.
In May the SEC put out its first draft of the changes, which could put less-regulated systems under heavier SEC scrutiny.

The proposals would cover the regulation of securities trading systems that would work via the internet and other computer-operated systems, including Instinet, a trading system for instituional customers that is owned by Reuters Holdings .
Bond market players want to see if the proposals would also change trading in government securities, municipal bonds and corporate bonds through the inter-dealer market, Saltzman said.

"The debt markets are exceedingly liquid and we are not aware of any systemic problems that require wholesale rethinking," Saltzman said, adding that much of the SEC's proposals speak really to the structure of the equities markets.

"There is no question that the inter-dealer broker system is critical and I think the SEC has recognized any regulation that impedes the ability of the interdealer system would not be looked upon favorably," he said.
Despite his concerns, Saltzman said PSA has not taken a formal position on the SEC's proposals outlined in the May release.
